# adhal

> adhal is an open-source, one-shot, peer-to-peer file drop between two devices. The receiver shows a five-word code (or QR), the sender types it, and the file travels directly between the two machines over the Holepunch DHT, end-to-end encrypted. No server stores the file and no account is needed.

- Install: `npm install --global @ad-hal/cli` (Node.js 24+, macOS or Linux)
- Receive: `ad-hal-receive --new ~/Downloads`
- Send: `ad-hal-send - ./file` (then type the code at the prompt)
- License: MIT. Published by Nebarti, LLC.
- Official packages: `@ad-hal/cli` and `@ad-hal/engine` only.

## How it works

- Peers find each other on HyperDHT and hole-punch through NAT; no port forwarding.
- Two words of the code name a public DHT topic; the other three are the password to a CPace PAKE, so guesses can only be made online.
- Every byte after the handshake is sealed with ChaCha20-Poly1305 under keys from the PAKE.
- The receiver sees name, size and SHA-256 before accepting; files are verified and never overwrite existing ones.
- Streams of unknown length (`tar c dir | ad-hal-send ...`) and resume of interrupted transfers are supported.

## Limits

- Not anonymous: each side's IP address is visible to the other and to nearby DHT nodes.
- The drop code is a bearer capability; share it privately.
- Windows is not yet supported for security purposes. The relay (`--relay=<key>`) is experimental.
